title: Kairos: Low-latency Multi-Agent Serving with Shared LLMs and Excessive Loads in the Public Cloud
technique: workflow orchestrator + workflow-aware priority scheduler (remaining-latency ordering) + memory-aware time-slot dispatcher over shared vLLM instances

optimized_metrics.evidence: Kairos, a multi-agent orchestration system that optimizes end-to-end latency for multi-agent applications.
To reduce end-to-end tail latency, Kairos prioritizes requests that have already experienced longer delays in prior stages.
The scheduler decides the serving priority of the requests based on their latency characteristics to reduce the overall queuing.
The dispatcher dispatches the requests to different LLM instances based on their memory demands to avoid GPU overloading.

headline_claim.text: Kairos reduces end-to-end latency by 17.8% to 28.4% compared to state-of-the-art works.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: This metric is defined as the end-to-end response time divided by the number of tokens generated, with lower values indicating better performance.
metric_definitions.notes: actually a length-normalized per-program latency (s/token over the whole multi-agent workflow); average and tail (P90/P95/P99) reported

load_regime: controlled load levels via average queueing-time ratio (0%-90% of e2e time) and request-rate sweep; inter-arrival distribution simulated from real trace
workloads: three multi-agent apps: QA, report generation, code generation (GSM8K/MMLU/MathQA, HumanEval etc.)
extractor_notes: Metric is length-normalized program latency; I coded as PROGRAM_JCT (could also be NORM_LAT). Mean is primary; tail is explicit design motivation (intra-agent priority).
